done.why: I was halfway through fetching the skeleton key from the studio to unlock the grating under the leaves, standing at the edge of the chasm, when the world told me I had used all 150 turns it allows. I was not finished; I had a plan and a target.

about: A treasure hunt around and under a boarded-up white house. You squeeze in through a window, find a trap door under the rug, and go hunting for things to lock in the trophy case in the living room: a painting, a bag of coins off a dead adventurer in a maze, a jewelled egg in a bird's nest. But the place is half under renovation (passages 'not finished', scenery 'closed for repairs' with notes from The Management) and somebody unseen keeps barring the trap door behind you every time you go down, so the only way home with your loot is a chimney that fits you, your lamp, and one thing more.

moments.note: Asked to read the leaflet and it quietly picked it up for me: '(Taken)'. Handy, but I didn't ask.
'walk around to the back of the house' got 'You can't see any such thing' while standing next to the house. Learned I have to say directions.
'climb through the window' just worked, exactly as I'd say it to a person.
Trap door crashes shut and someone bars it behind me. Sword starts glowing. Trapped underground, immediately.
One swing and the troll's out cold. I felt dangerous.
East passage 'has not been finished', with a note: 'Back soon. -- The Management.' Laughed out loud; the place is under construction.
Chimney refuses me with a clear, fair rule: room for me, a light, and one thing more. I knew exactly what to do.
Trophy case 'has the patient air of something that expects to be filled.' Made me want to fill it.
Dust on the trap door scuffed by 'somebody's comings and goings'. Who is down there?
Barred in again. I'd half hoped it was a one-time thing.
'a dark that your lamp does not so much light as annoy' - best line of the night.
I could 'look at the chasm' but 'tie the rope to the edge of the chasm' and 'climb down into the chasm' both got 'You can't see any such thing'. Felt like it was pretending not to understand.
My leaflet is in the first maze room though I dropped it after going north. So north looped me back. Took a moment to believe it.
Came east into a dead end, can't go west back out. The maze does not respect where I came from.
A skeleton, a skeleton key, and a bag bulging with coins. Treasure two, and a warning.
Went up into the skeleton room, can't go down out of it. Started to feel the maze closing.
Found my leaflet again. Real relief; the breadcrumbs paid off.
'how am I doing?' - 'That sentence isn't one I recognize.' I wanted a tally and didn't know the word for it.
'CANYON VIEW CLOSED FOR REPAIRS. The Frobozz Magic Scenery Company regrets any inconvenience.' The renovation joke keeps paying off.
Jewelled egg in a nest 'scavenged by a childless songbird'. Treasure three, up a tree.
Leaves 'swept together on purpose' hide a grating. Somebody's been tidying up after themselves out here too.
Grating's locked and I'd dropped the skeleton key in the studio to fit up the chimney. My own doing.
Turn cap hit at the chasm edge, one room short of the key. So close.

wished: Ask in plain words how I was doing or what my treasures were worth; 'how am I doing?' wasn't understood and I didn't know another way to say it.
Use the rope at the chasm. I had a rope and a bottomless drop and the world wouldn't let me put them together.
Go back the way I came in the maze. Walking east into a dead end and then not being able to walk west out of it felt like cheating.
Tell one dead end from another. With no markers left I couldn't tell if I'd been somewhere before.
Find out who keeps barring the trap door. The scuffed dust and the barring happened three times and I never caught a glimpse.
Get through the grating under the leaves; I had the key located and the turns ran out.
Go east past the troll room or out to the Canyon View; both were closed off with notes, which was funny once but I still wanted in.

lines.line: The passage to the east has not been finished. A note is pinned to the rock: "Back soon. -- The Management."
lines.why: First sign the place was being run by someone, and funny. It set the tone for everything after.

lines.line: The chimney has room for you, a light to climb by and one thing more, and not an inch besides.
lines.why: A refusal that told me exactly how to fix it. That's the kind of 'no' I can work with, and it shaped every trip home.

lines.line: It has the patient air of something that expects to be filled.
lines.why: Turned the trophy case from furniture into my goal.

lines.line: The dust on it has been scuffed and smeared by somebody's comings and goings, and nobody has thought to sweep it.
lines.why: Made the barring feel like a person, not a mechanism.

lines.line: The chasm drops away from your feet into a dark that your lamp does not so much light as annoy. A pebble kicked over the edge is never heard from again. Neither, by the look of it, was whoever kicked the last one.
lines.why: The best writing in the place, and it made me want to try the rope, which hurt a bit when the rope went nowhere.

lines.line: Whatever he came into the maze looking for, the maze found him first.
lines.why: I was lost at the time, carrying his coins. It landed.

lines.line: CANYON VIEW CLOSED FOR REPAIRS. The Frobozz Magic Scenery Company regrets any inconvenience.
lines.why: The renovation joke, done again and better; by now I believed in a Management.

fun.why: Three real treasures found and locked away, a troll flattened in one swing, and jokes that kept landing. The chasm rope dead end and the one-way maze cost it the fifth point.

engagement.why: I never idled. The maze had me dropping breadcrumbs and reasoning about loops, and the locked grating gave me a plan I was still executing when the turns ran out.

difficulty.why: Right. The chimney rule and the troll were fair and clear; the maze was hard but beatable with markers; the chasm was the one place I felt the world was unfair rather than hard.

interestingness.why: The idea that someone is managing and closing off this place, barring doors and sweeping leaves over gratings, ran under everything and I never got to the bottom of it. The maze itself was less interesting than the signs of who else had been in it.

prose.why: Mostly brisk and plain, which suited me as a newcomer, with sudden sharp lines about the chasm, the skeleton, the trophy case, and the leaves. The maze rooms being word-for-word identical was deliberate but wearing.
